description: 120-Item Calibrated Adaptive Question Tree & Epistemic Blind-Inference Bank (12 Core Anchors, 40 Conditional Branch Probes, 40 DeYoung 2PL IRT Deep-Resolution Items, and 28 Disarming Everyday Behavioral Micro-Questions).

items.text: When I’m learning something new, I naturally look for the deeper pattern of how it all fits together before worrying about the small details.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures top-down generative model compression in dorsolateral PFC prior to bottom-up detail encoding.

items.text: A small shift in the light in a room, a piece of music, or someone’s tone of voice can stay with me for a long time.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures aesthetic and sensory absorption across positive and neutral valence to de-confound perceptual sensitivity from threat vigilance.

items.text: Simple everyday errands can sit on my list for days, yet when a question or project truly fascinates me, hours pass like minutes.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Symmetry-breaking probe separating striatal interest-gated hyperfocus (ADHD/AuDHD dopamine foraging) from low trait motivation.

items.text: My mind feels noticeably calmer when my space is tidy and I know what the next few days look like.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Assesses environmental entropy suppression and temporal predictability preference.

items.text: When two conversations are happening at the same table, both voices reach me at almost the same volume—I feel much more at ease talking one-on-one.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Separates auditory cocktail-party stream-segregation cost (monotropic sensory precision) from true social anhedonia.

items.text: If a group of friends or coworkers is unsure what to do next, I feel comfortable gently stepping in to guide the plan.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures dopaminergic social agency and comfort navigating the hippocampal power/initiative axis.

items.text: In a disagreement with someone I care about, making sure we both feel heard matters more to me than winning the point.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Evaluates anterior insula/mPFC allostatic coupling vs. decoupled adversarial point-scoring.

items.text: I appreciate when people say exactly what they mean, rather than wrapping the truth in polite hints.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Distinguishes low-context literal communication clarity from interpersonal coldness.

items.text: Even when things are going well, part of my mind quietly thinks ahead to what might need protecting.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures hippocampal-septal anticipatory uncertainty vigilance and protective simulation.

items.text: When plans change suddenly, I usually find my footing quickly without feeling thrown off for long.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures serotonergic prediction-error buffering during unexpected state transitions.

items.text: People around me see me as steady and on top of things, though they rarely see how much quiet effort it takes me behind the scenes.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Quantifies prefrontal compensatory scaffolding and executive masking cost (M).

items.text: Compared to times in my life when I’ve felt most rested and at ease, these past couple of weeks have felt heavier or more tiring.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Differential state probe isolating transient allostatic load S_state(t) from lifelong trait wiring.

items.text: Having 20+ open browser tabs or saved links feels more like a cozy library of possibilities than clutter I need to clear right away.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Disarming ecological behavioral proxy for exploratory novelty foraging vs. linear closure (Anchor C r = -0.61, Salience-Split r = +0.64) that bypasses self-evaluative shame around 'messiness'.

items.text: When sending a short text like 'Sounds good', I often add an exclamation point, emoji, or 'haha' just so a plain period doesn't accidentally read as cold.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Disarming digital pragmatics proxy for interpersonal allostatic cushioning and affiliative tone regulation (Anchor A r = +0.58, Compensatory Masking r = +0.44).

items.text: When a social plan I genuinely wanted to go to gets canceled at the last minute, my very first physical reaction is a quiet wave of relief.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Decouples affiliative care ('genuinely wanted to go') from autonomic transition & sensory saturation cost (Anchor E r = -0.63, Acoustic Stream Split r = +0.59).

items.text: When someone explains a new idea, my mind automatically connects it to something from a completely different area of life—like seeing how a kitchen recipe works just like a piece of music.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Probes cross-domain analogical mapping in frontopolar cortex when initial pattern-seeking (Q1) is elevated.

items.text: Rather than talking about big theories for an hour, I understand things best when someone shows me a real, working example I can try with my own hands.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Confirms high sensory-evidence precision and procedural grounding when abstract prior preference is low.

items.text: Even when I don’t picture a detailed visual scene in my head, I can instantly feel the invisible structure of how an idea, a machine, or a story holds together.
items.scientific_hypothesis: De-confounds non-visual conceptual imagination in low-V1 imagery responders.

items.text: When someone describes a place they visited, my mind automatically builds the room—the texture of the table, the time of day, and the atmosphere around them.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Evaluates high-gain perceptual simulation when Mind's Eye vividness is elevated.

items.text: When I look at a complicated problem or a messy situation, I usually sense the whole shape of it at once before I can explain the steps out loud.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Links rapid spatial chunking in Night Sky telemetry to intuitive Gestalt system synthesis.

items.text: My best ideas rarely arrive on a schedule; they show up when I have unhurried room to wander, tinker, and follow a thread wherever it leads.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Resolves high-exploration temperature foraging when Openness substantially exceeds Conscientiousness.

items.text: A quiet evening spent diving deep into a topic, craft, or story leaves me feeling more energized than a lively night out with a crowd.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Distinguishes rich internal cortical simulation from low social reward foraging.

parent_trigger.label: Deep Inner World (O) vs Quiet Social Battery (E)

items.text: Because I take in so many subtle details in a room—the lighting, the mood, the background sounds—beauty moves me deeply, even if chaotic spaces tire me out faster.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Separates high-gain sensory processing sensitivity (HSP) from pure emotional dysregulation.

items.text: A task that felt impossible to start for a week can suddenly get finished in a single locked-in afternoon once it becomes urgent or interesting.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Tests catecholaminergic urgency/novelty ignition following a high Q3 salience-split response.

items.text: Even when a task is dry or repetitive, I find a quiet satisfaction in chipping away at it a little bit each day until it’s done.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Confirms high tonic striatal goal maintenance independent of novelty spikes.

items.text: If I put something away in a closed drawer, I risk forgetting it exists—keeping active things visible where my eyes land on them works better for my brain.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Distinguishes working-memory externalization ('out of sight, out of mind') from carelessness.

items.text: To keep from dropping the ball on commitments, I rely on alarms, lists, or quiet rituals that nobody else realizes I need.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Probes prosthetic executive scaffolding in high-masking individuals.

items.text: My energy works more like a wave than a thermostat—when a fresh challenge catches my eye, I move fast and do my best thinking on the fly.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Cross-validates high RT coefficient of variation / phasic arousal in Still Water with adaptive sprint behavior.

items.text: Before I commit to a decision or send off an important message, I naturally pause to double-check the details so I only have to do it once.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Links cautious drift-diffusion decision thresholds in Still Water to high error-monitoring precision.

items.text: I crave fresh ideas and variety in what I’m learning, yet I feel much safer when my physical surroundings and daily anchor points stay predictable.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Detects dual-attractor coexistence of high novelty drive and high environmental sameness need.

items.text: The first 80% of a project—figuring out the puzzle and seeing that it works—is thrilling to me, while the final 20% of polishing and filing takes three times the willpower.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Quantifies reward-prediction-error decay once epistemic uncertainty is resolved.

items.text: Even though noisy rooms drain me quickly, I can talk for three hours straight with one trusted person about something we both care about and walk away glowing.
items.scientific_hypothesis: De-confounds intact dyadic social reward (ventral striatal/oxytocin warmth) from multi-speaker acoustic fatigue.

items.text: Walking into a lively gathering, a busy café, or a shared workspace gives my mood an immediate lift.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Confirms exogenous dopaminergic arousal up-regulation in high-stimulation social environments.

items.text: I rarely try to be the loudest voice in the room; I prefer to let my work, preparation, or a calm suggestion speak for itself.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Distinguishes low dominance-display preference from lack of personal competence.

items.text: When a situation gets confusing or urgent, I actually feel calmer once I’m helping organize who does what.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures high agency and executive coordination under social uncertainty.

items.text: People who meet me often think I’m more outgoing than I really am because I’m warm and attentive in the moment—even though I need quiet time alone afterward to recharge.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Separates high affiliative empathy (Agreeableness) from social energy expenditure (Extraversion).

items.text: Half of my best realizations happen mid-sentence while talking an idea through with someone I trust.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures dialogic externalized working-memory processing.

parent_trigger.label: High Social Energy (E) vs Flexible Structure (C)

items.text: One of my favorite ways to be close to someone is simply being in the same room doing our own things—reading, working, or cooking—without needing to fill the silence.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Probes low-demand co-regulation ('parallel play') affinity in sensory-selective profiles.

items.text: At a gathering, I naturally notice who might get along or who is standing on the edge of the room, and I enjoy bringing them into the conversation.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures prosocial network bridging when both Extraversion and Agreeableness are elevated.

parent_trigger.label: High Social Energy + High Warmth (E+A Catalyst)

items.text: If someone walks into the room carrying unspoken stress or sadness, I feel it in my own body almost before they say a word.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Assesses high anterior insula interoceptive mirror resonance.

parent_trigger.label: Q7 ≥ 4 (High care for mutual feeling heard)

items.text: To me, giving someone a clear, honest answer—without sugarcoating or making them guess—is one of the most respectful ways to show I care.
items.scientific_hypothesis: De-confounds direct epistemic benevolence from interpersonal antagonism.

items.text: When I need to give feedback or say no, I instinctively look for a gentle way to phrase it so the other person never feels embarrassed or cornered.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures proactive interpersonal friction buffering and face-saving care.

items.text: When someone I love is overwhelmed, my first instinct is to help them map out a practical fix or take a chore off their plate rather than just talking about the feelings.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Distinguishes instrumental acts-of-service care from low empathy.

items.text: Even when setting a boundary is completely reasonable, part of me still replays the conversation afterward wondering if I was too firm.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures post-boundary guilt and relational hyper-responsibility when A and N co-activate.

parent_trigger.label: High Warmth + High Sensitivity (A+N Boundary Replay)

items.text: I treat everyone with warmth, but if a rule or authority figure is clearly unfair, I have a hard time nodding along just to keep the peace.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Separates principled fairness advocacy from arbitrary defiance.

parent_trigger.label: High Independent Inquiry (O) vs Normative Compliance (A)

items.text: Friends or coworkers often end up telling me things they haven’t told anyone else, simply because they sense I won’t judge them.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Identifies quiet dyadic sanctuary providers.

parent_trigger.label: High 1-on-1 Warmth (A) vs Quiet Social Battery (E)

items.text: Before hitting send on an important message, I often read it back in the other person’s shoes to make sure the tone feels warm and clear.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Validates mentalizing perspective-taking behind digital punctuation habits.

parent_trigger.label: Q14 ≥ 4 (Uses warmth cushions in short texts)

items.text: Before a big trip, presentation, or hard conversation, my mind naturally runs through three or four 'what-if' branches so I won’t be caught off guard.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Probes anticipatory model-based tree search in high-vigilance planners.

parent_trigger.label: Q9 ≥ 4 (Quietly thinks ahead to what needs protecting)

items.text: Once I’ve done what I reasonably can for tomorrow, my mind lets go of the problem easily and trusts that I’ll handle whatever happens in the moment.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Confirms low baseline behavioral inhibition system (BIS) gain.

items.text: When a plan I’ve already mentally prepared for changes at the last minute, I need ten quiet minutes to reset my internal map before I can jump into the new plan.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Distinguishes cognitive set-shifting/predictive-prior updating cost from interpersonal anger.

items.text: Strangely enough, when an actual emergency happens, my mind often gets unusually clear and steady—and only feels tired after the crisis is over.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures acute noradrenergic clarity and emotional buffering under high-salience stress.

parent_trigger.label: Q10 ≥ 4 (Finds footing quickly when plans change)

items.text: What looks like 'irritability' from the outside is almost always just my senses hitting full capacity from too much noise, bright light, or competing demands at once.
items.scientific_hypothesis: De-confounds sensory allostatic overload from primary affective volatility.

items.text: When I’m running on empty after a demanding stretch of life, small hurdles feel ten times steeper than they do when I’ve had a real weekend to rest.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Calibrates state-dependent prediction-error inflation during depleted epochs.

items.text: Hours after a social event, my brain will sometimes replay a single moment where I wonder if I said the right thing.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Links social masking expenditure to post-event DMN self-monitoring.

items.text: My shoulders, jaw, or stomach often notice that I’m stressed a full hour before my conscious mind admits it.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures somatic interoceptive lead-time in high-sensitivity profiles.

items.text: When something in my daily life breaks or acts up, I like figuring out why it happened rather than just ignoring it.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) O_intellect discriminator separating basic causal curiosity from passive disengagement.

items.text: I enjoy conversations that dig into how systems, people, or history actually work beneath the surface.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) O_intellect probe for everyday explanatory depth.

items.text: For fun, I often catch myself building mental models of complex topics—testing where an argument holds up and where it falls apart.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) O_intellect probe for spontaneous epistemic model-testing.

items.text: Nothing feels quite as exhilarating as untangling a deep paradox or synthesizing three seemingly unrelated fields into one clear framework.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.18) O_intellect probe resolving extreme upper-tail abstract systemizing.

items.text: A good song, a warm sunset, or a well-cooked meal can noticeably brighten my mood.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) O_openness probe establishing baseline aesthetic receptivity.

items.text: I’m drawn to stories, places, and music that have a slightly bittersweet, mysterious, or poetic feeling to them.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) O_openness probe for complex aesthetic valence.

items.text: Sometimes a piece of art, a film, or a quiet moment in nature absorbs me so completely that I lose track of time and my surroundings.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) O_openness probe measuring Tellegen-style perceptual absorption.

items.text: My dreams, daydreams, and sensory impressions are so rich and layered that they often feel like a second creative life running alongside my waking day.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.15) O_openness probe for extreme upper-tail DMN aesthetic immersion.

items.text: When people are counting on me for something important, I make sure I show up and get the core job done.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) C_industriousness probe for baseline reliability.

items.text: Once I decide what needs doing for the day, I can usually get started without waiting around to 'feel inspired.'
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) C_industriousness probe for low task-initiation friction.

items.text: Even on a long, multi-month goal with zero immediate applause, I keep a steady rhythm week after week until I cross the finish line.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) C_industriousness probe for temporal discounting resistance.

items.text: Distractions rarely pull me off course; I can sustain calm, disciplined execution on hard, unglamorous work for hours at a time.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.16) C_industriousness probe resolving extreme upper-tail executive persistence.

items.text: I know where my essential everyday items—like keys, wallet, or phone—are when I need to head out the door.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) C_orderliness baseline probe.

items.text: After cooking a meal or finishing a project, I like resetting the space so I don’t wake up to yesterday’s mess.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) C_orderliness probe for daily state closure.

items.text: I naturally organize my files, tools, or schedule into clear categories so everything has a home and nothing slips through the cracks.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) C_orderliness probe for proactive taxonomic organization.

items.text: Even a small visual crookedness or an unlogged detail jumps out at me immediately—bringing order and symmetry to a system feels deeply satisfying.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.12) C_orderliness probe for high environmental precision.

items.text: Sharing a good laugh or a warm moment with someone I trust makes my whole day feel lighter.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) E_enthusiasm probe for baseline social reward sensitivity.

items.text: When something good happens in my life, one of my first impulses is to share the news with a friend or family member.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) E_enthusiasm probe for affiliative capitalization.

items.text: I warm up to new people quickly, and my enthusiasm tends to make conversations feel lively and effortless.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) E_enthusiasm probe for spontaneous social approach.

items.text: Being around people, music, and shared celebration charges my battery so much that I’m often one of the last people ready for the night to end.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.14) E_enthusiasm probe for upper-tail extraverted reward gain.

items.text: If someone gets my order wrong or overlooks me in line, I can politely speak up for myself.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) E_assertiveness probe for basic self-advocacy.

items.text: In a meeting or group chat, I don’t hesitate to offer a clear proposal when everyone else is hesitating.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) E_assertiveness probe for group initiative.

items.text: I naturally gravitate toward roles where I can set the vision, rally people around a goal, and make the tough calls.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) E_assertiveness probe for leadership agency.

items.text: Even in a room full of strong personalities or high stakes, I feel completely in my element steering the room and negotiating the outcome.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.17) E_assertiveness probe for upper-tail social agency.

items.text: When someone close to me is having a rough day, I genuinely care about helping them feel a little less alone.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) A_compassion baseline probe.

items.text: I often notice the quiet person in a group who keeps getting talked over, and I make a point of asking what they were going to say.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) A_compassion probe for attentive inclusion.

items.text: Even when someone is acting prickly or defensive, I naturally find myself wondering what hurt or exhaustion they might be carrying underneath.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) A_compassion probe for compassionate mentalizing under friction.

items.text: Other people’s joy and pain feel so real to me that tending to the wellbeing of the people and creatures around me is a central compass of my life.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.19) A_compassion probe for upper-tail allostatic altruism.

items.text: I believe basic courtesy—saying thank you, respecting shared spaces, and not cutting corners at someone else’s expense—matters every day.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) A_politeness baseline probe.

items.text: Even when I’m frustrated, I avoid taking cheap shots or making someone look bad in front of others.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) A_politeness probe for antagonistic impulse restraint.

items.text: When a disagreement heats up, I instinctively lower my voice and look for common ground rather than escalating the tension.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) A_politeness probe for normative conflict de-escalation.

items.text: I almost never feel tempted to pull rank, bluff, or bend the rules for my own advantage—playing fair and honoring everyone’s dignity comes before winning.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.11) A_politeness probe for upper-tail cooperative fairness.

items.text: When something really matters to me—a relationship, a health question, or a big change—I naturally feel a flicker of nervousness before it’s resolved.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) N_withdrawal baseline probe.

items.text: When I’m facing an uncertain situation, I tend to hang back and observe until I feel sure of the footing.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) N_withdrawal probe for cautious approach inhibition.

items.text: If I make a mistake or sense that someone might be disappointed in me, that heavy feeling can linger in my chest for the rest of the day.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) N_withdrawal probe for internalizing error sensitivity.

items.text: Even when nothing is actively wrong, my mind often feels like it’s scanning the horizon for the next shoe to drop, making deep rest hard to reach.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.18) N_withdrawal probe for upper-tail hyper-vigilant withdrawal.

items.text: When I’m hungry, sleep-deprived, or interrupted three times in a row, my patience wears noticeably thinner.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Low-threshold (b=-1.50) N_volatility baseline probe.

items.text: When technology glitches or a simple task goes sideways at the worst moment, a quick flash of frustration hits me right away.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-low threshold (b=-0.60) N_volatility probe for frustrated goal-blocking reactivity.

items.text: When I feel misunderstood or treated unfairly, my emotions surge so strongly that it takes real effort not to let them spill out immediately.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Moderate-high threshold (b=+0.60) N_volatility probe for affective surge amplitude.

items.text: My emotional weather can shift from bright to stormy in minutes when plans unravel or tension spikes, and it takes hours for my nervous system to fully settle again.
items.scientific_hypothesis: High-threshold (b=+1.50, a=2.16) N_volatility probe for upper-tail autonomic recovery latency.

items.text: I have a dedicated chair, hook, or corner for clothes that aren’t dirty enough for the laundry but aren’t quite ready to go back in the closet.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Ecological proxy for intermediate state-buffering vs. binary categorical closure in everyday spaces.

items.text: When a song, album, or flavor hits the exact right nerve, I can happily play or eat it on repeat dozens of times until I’ve soaked up every drop of it.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures monotropic sensory-aesthetic acoustic savoring and predictable dopaminergic groove regulation.

items.text: Before making a simple phone call—like booking an appointment or calling a business—I often mentally rehearse my opening sentence before hitting dial.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Disarming behavioral indicator of anticipatory social-pragmatic scripting and uncertainty reduction.

items.text: I frequently misjudge how long the 'getting out the door' steps—shoes, keys, water bottle, traffic—actually take, turning a ten-minute buffer into a two-minute scramble.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Ecological time-blindness / transition-substep compression proxy for striatal temporal estimation.

items.text: I have looked up one quick question late at night and found myself forty-five minutes later reading deep into the history of lighthouses, deep-sea cables, or ancient bread.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures spontaneous intrinsic epistemic foraging when external task demands are offline.

items.text: After getting home from work, errands, or a social event, I sometimes sit quietly in the parked car or by the entryway for five extra minutes before going inside.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures autonomic state-transition buffering between external social roles and home space.

items.text: Seeing little red unread notification badges on my phone or inbox bugs me enough that I clear them almost as soon as they appear.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Digital micro-proxy for open-loop intolerance and visual entropy suppression.

items.text: Before going to a new restaurant or café, I almost always look up the menu or photos ahead of time so I already know the vibe and what I want.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Everyday environmental prior-seeding behavior that reduces on-the-spot sensory and choice load.

items.text: Even when the audio is perfectly clear and in my native language, I prefer watching shows or videos with the subtitles turned on.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Cross-modal orthographic-auditory anchoring proxy associated with auditory stream precision.

items.text: If someone bumps into me in a narrow aisle—or if I brush past a coat rack—my mouth says 'Oops, sorry!' before my brain even checks whose fault it was.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures hyper-automatized interpersonal friction smoothing and allostatic peace-keeping.

items.text: Walking into a room with a harsh overhead 'big light' makes me immediately want to switch it off and turn on a couple of warm lamps instead.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Everyday psychophysical proxy for visual sensory gain and atmospheric sensitivity.

items.text: Instead of reading one book or learning one skill strictly from start to finish, I usually have three or four going at once depending on what my curiosity wants that day.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures parallel epistemic foraging across multiple active conceptual threads.

items.text: When catching up with a close friend, I love sending or receiving rambling three-minute voice notes that feel like a miniature podcast between the two of us.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures high-warmth asynchronous vocal prosody connection.

items.text: For a trip, I pack a written checklist and have my bag mostly ready the night before, rather than tossing things in an hour before leaving.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Concrete behavioral anchor for prospective planning vs. deadline-driven mobilization.

items.text: I often read a message from someone I care about, compose a thoughtful reply in my head, and then realize three days later that I never actually typed and sent it.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures internal simulation completion substituting for motor-output closure in high-salience minds.

items.text: Folding laundry, washing dishes, or cleaning the kitchen goes twice as smoothly if I have a familiar podcast, audiobook, or comfort show playing in the background.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Ecological proxy for tonic dopamine scaffolding ('auditory body-doubling') during low-stimulation chores.

items.text: If someone who usually texts warmly suddenly replies with a one-word 'Okay.' with a period at the end, my brain immediately wonders if something is wrong.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures high interpersonal prediction-error gain on micro-pragmatic cues.

items.text: When I’m cooking, I naturally wash bowls and wipe the counter as I go, rather than leaving a mountain of pans for after dinner.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Everyday behavioral measure of real-time working-memory and spatial entropy regulation.

items.text: Spotting a dog trotting happily down the sidewalk or a toddler waving from a grocery cart automatically puts a genuine smile on my face.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Unconfounded behavioral proxy for spontaneous affiliative warmth and positive resonance.

items.text: If a shopping cart is blocking the walkway or a group needs someone to ask a question at the counter, I just step up and handle it without waiting for someone else to.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures everyday environmental agency and low bystander-hesitation threshold.

items.text: Over the years, I’ve gone through intense seasons of diving deep into a brand-new hobby, craft, or subject—learning all the tools and lingo—before eventually moving on to a new fascination.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures high-gain epistemic exploration cycles across the lifespan.

items.text: A scratchy shirt tag, a flickering fluorescent bulb, or a repetitive tapping sound in the room can pull at my attention until I fix it or step away.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Psychophysical proxy for reduced sensory habituation (low gating of repetitive bottom-up inputs).

items.text: Friends or family members often ask me to help them word a tricky text or email because I know how to make it sound both clear and kind.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Ecological validation of high diplomatic pragmatics and relational mentalizing.

items.text: In the first half hour after waking up, I love having a quiet cup of coffee or tea and easing into the day before jumping into lively conversation.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Captures gradual cortical arousal ramp-up preference vs. immediate high-stimulation engagement.

items.text: Halfway through watching a mystery or movie, part of my brain is already noticing the writer’s clues and predicting how the ending is going to fit together.
items.scientific_hypothesis: Measures spontaneous top-down predictive structure tracking during narrative immersion.
